name: addERI_Proxmox_VE
description: Sets an ERI on each Proxmox VE node's resource so Proxmox_VE_Topology can attach its node vertex to it. Needs no API token.
technicalNotes:
OPTIONAL, and off by default. Applies to any resource carrying pve.topology.enabled=true (lowercase) -- set it on every Proxmox node's resource, typically on the group that holds them, together with pve.topology.cluster. Set both on a group holding only that cluster's nodes, never on a broad or dynamic group such as "Linux Servers", or this module stamps a node key on every server in it. Proxmox_VE_Topology shares the opt-in property and is only useful with this module.

Deliberately not gated on hasCategory("ProxmoxVE"): that category needs the API token, and the map needs this key on every node, while the token belongs on one node per cluster (docs/INSTALL.md 4.1). So the key comes from the API where the resource has a token, and otherwise from properties: pve.topology.cluster, and the node name from pve.topology.node or else the short form of system.sysname or system.hostname (Proxmox requires a node's name to be its hostname). A resource whose hostname is an IP address needs pve.topology.node. Without a cluster name it stays silent. The token-holding resource publishes the exact name to copy as auto.pve.cluster.name.

Stamps one ERI key, in its own category "proxmoxve" so it combines with the MAC-based ERIs a monitored Linux resource already carries rather than replacing them -- keys from every category merge into predef.externalResourceID, and the resource type comes from the highest-priority entry across all categories (docs/DESIGN.md 7, spike 1). This module emits PhysicalServer, the type a node already has, so the priority does not change what it is drawn as.

The key is synthesised from the cluster and node names because Proxmox exposes no hardware identifier for a node anywhere in its API: /cluster/status gives name, ip and nodeid, /nodes/{node}/status gives none, and /nodes/{node}/network has no hwaddr. VMware does not need this because vCenter hands out each ESXi host's hardware UUID. pveTopoKey in the preamble is the single definition of the key's shape, and Proxmox_VE_Topology calls the same helper -- the two must produce byte-identical keys or every node vertex silently stops matching its resource.

The node it stamps is the one the resource is, not any node in the cluster: on the API path /cluster/status marks the responding node with local=true; on the property path the resource's own hostname names it. Without that, every node would be stamped with the same key.

Silent on any failure, like addCategory_Proxmox_VE: it runs against resources that may not be Proxmox, and a PropertySource that prints on a host it does not understand corrupts that resource's properties.
